data.agro_ecological_zone: Sudano-Sahelian Peanut Basin of Senegal (Kaolack region)
data.adaptation_notes: Best suited to the sandy to sandy-loam, well-drained soils common in the Kaolack Peanut Basin. Sow immediately after the first effective rains (≥25–30 mm over 2–3 days), ensure weed-free conditions through 40–45 days after planting, and avoid waterlogging. Apply basal phosphorus and calcium (e.g., SSP/DAP at planting; gypsum at early pegging) to enhance pod fill and quality. Optimal rainfall window is roughly 500–800 mm with a 90–120 day growing period typical for Kaolack; fields with light-textured, friable topsoil facilitate pegging and pod development.
data.normal_planting_window: Late June to early July at onset of rains in Kaolack

data.adaptation_notes: 28-206 is an early-maturing erect/bunch peanut suited to the central Groundnut Basin’s sandy to sandy-loam, well-drained soils. Best performance occurs with timely planting at the onset of rains, adequate calcium (gypsum) at pegging, and phosphorus fertilization on low-P soils. Its early maturity helps it escape late-season drought and end-of-rains disease pressure, making it suitable for the variable rainfall of Kaolack. Because it is generally susceptible to rosette and leaf spots, integrated management (healthy seed, early planting, aphid management to limit rosette, and timely fungicide sprays where feasible) is recommended.

data.adaptation_notes: ICGV 91114 is a Spanish-bunch, medium-duration, drought-tolerant groundnut suited to the Sudano-Sahelian Peanut Basin, including Kaolack. It performs well under end-of-season (terminal) drought and erratic rainfall, typical of the region. Best results are obtained on light, well-drained sandy to sandy-loam soils with adequate calcium at pegging, good weed control during the first 30-40 days, and timely harvest to avoid pod sprouting and aflatoxin risk. Avoid waterlogging and heavy clays. In Kaolack, align planting with the reliable onset of rains (late June–July) and harvest before late-season dry spells intensify (October–November).
